Home News Arts and Culture Business Sports Opinion Research Live TV/Radio Media Elections Dark Mode Dark mode --> National Asikuma Inland Port to ease Tema Port congestion and create jobs in Asuogyaman – Mahama Source : Maxwell Agbagba 22 November 2026 5:01pm ▶ Listen to this article Audio By Carbonatix
President John Mahama says the construction of the Asikuma Inland Port will help ease congestion at the Tema Port while creating jobs and opening up economic opportunities for residents of Asuogyaman.
He says the facility, sponsored by LMI and financed by the International Finance Corporation (IFC), will serve as the southern terminal of the Volta Lake transport system when completed.
Speaking at the Odwira Akyi Akwasidae Kese and the 15th anniversary of the enstoolment of Odeneho Kwafo Akoto III as Akwamuhene, President Mahama said the project will be supported by an extension of the railway line from Mpakadan to Asikuma.
He explained that containers and other imports will be transported by rail from Tema to Asikuma, where they will be loaded onto barges and moved along the Volta River to Debre in the northern part of Ghana.
According to the President, the arrangement will provide a more seamless transportation route for Ghana's northern neighbours in the Sahel, particularly Burkina Faso, allowing them to move goods without having to travel all the way to Tema.
President Mahama said the development will not only reduce pressure on the Tema Port but also create opportunities for tourism and business through plans to establish a modern marina at Mpakadan.
"All these investments are going to create jobs for the young people of Asuogyaman," he said.
The President said the government will work closely with traditional authorities, the District Assembly, investors and local communities to ensure residents benefit directly from the development projects.
He stressed that development must translate into tangible benefits for the communities where such investments are undertaken.
"Development must not simply happen in our communities; it must happen for our communities," President Mahama stated.
He said his vision is to see Akwamu preserve its traditional heritage while embracing modern economic opportunities, adding that prosperity must be shared across all regions and communities.
Congratulating Odeneho Kwafo Akoto III on 15 years of leadership, the President wished him good health and wisdom, urging the current generation to build on the legacy of their forebears.
"Our ancestors built a kingdom of influence. Our generation must build an economy of opportunity," he said.
